headline: One HubSpot that Marketing, Sales, CS, and Finance all trust, with AI doing the manual work.
pitch: I run the systems and data under a revenue team. At flyExclusive I own HubSpot architecture and governance for the sales organization: lifecycle stages, required fields, ownership rules, deduplication, and Master Data Management. I also replaced the company's legacy website platform with a custom site that feeds quote requests straight into the CRM. I build the AI tools that take manual work off the team myself, including an LLM pipeline wired into the CRM that enriches records and scores leads, conversational reporting so teams can ask the data questions, and proposal and agreement tools that keep documents on-standard. Before that, at TRANZACT, I did attribution, forecasting, and experimentation with commercial and finance leadership. The common thread is tying every marketing and sales touch to revenue in a way Finance will sign off on.

requirements.need: Deep HubSpot expertise; own and architect core revenue systems
requirements.evidence: Led flyExclusive's CRM transformation on HubSpot: governance (properties, required fields, ownership rules, lifecycle stages), a scalable data architecture, deduplication workflows, and Master Data Management, giving the sales organization a single source of truth. I also built the integrations around it: website quote requests flow into the CRM, and CRM outcomes flow back to the ad platforms as offline conversions.

requirements.need: Hands-on experience with automation tools and AI solutions, including internal knowledge bases
requirements.evidence: At flyExclusive I engineered an autonomous pipeline connecting LLM APIs to the CRM database for enrichment, personalized outreach, and lead scoring. I also built conversational reporting interfaces and AI proposal and agreement tools for the sales team. The chat on this site's home page is an internal knowledge base in miniature: answers grounded in one source document, with an automated eval harness checking accuracy and refusals. I build all of this daily in Claude Code with MCP servers.

requirements.need: Diagnose funnel leaks; build dashboards, forecasting models, and predictive analytics
requirements.evidence: Redesigned flyExclusive's retail performance dashboards so leadership can see marketing's contribution through the funnel, and built an LLM-powered lead-scoring model that prioritizes high-value accounts. At TRANZACT I built forecasting models and measurement frameworks that fed executive recommendations on acquisition and pipeline growth.

requirements.need: Strong analytics skills: SQL, BI tools, executive dashboards
requirements.evidence: SQL daily for years, Python (pandas, scikit-learn), Databricks, Postgres, Tableau, and Power BI. I shipped a Python competitive-pricing app that directly informed flyExclusive's 2026 pricing tables.

requirements.need: Define data capture, structure, and governance across the customer lifecycle
requirements.evidence: This is the core of my flyExclusive role: lifecycle stages, required fields, ownership rules, identity resolution, and deduplication in HubSpot, plus conversion tracking from the first web visit (Google Tag Manager, Meta Conversions API, Google Ads) through to closed sales. On this site, a tracking taxonomy is enforced in code and every bad record is flagged and counted by rule instead of being silently dropped.

requirements.need: Marketing attribution and demand generation expertise
requirements.evidence: Multi-touch attribution at TRANZACT; attribution frameworks and offline conversion uploads at flyExclusive, so ad platforms optimize on qualified leads and sales rather than form fills. The worked framework on this site shows how I turn attribution into a budget decision.

requirements.need: Track record of evaluating, consolidating, or replacing GTM software
requirements.evidence: Migrated flyExclusive's website off its legacy CMS onto a custom-built site wired into the CRM and ad platforms, and consolidated duplicate CRM records into one governed system. A formal tool-stack audit and vendor consolidation across a full RevTech stack would be new scope for me.

requirements.need: 5–8+ years in RevOps, Sales Ops, GTM Systems, or Revenue Enablement, leading teams or major initiatives
requirements.evidence: Six years in marketing and data roles that support sales and revenue, leading major initiatives like flyExclusive's HubSpot transformation and website migration. My titles have been CRM analytics and marketing insights, not RevOps.

requirements.need: Billing or subscription platform experience (Chargebee), including revenue recognition
requirements.evidence: I haven't run Chargebee or a billing platform. My route in would be the data model: map how Chargebee subscriptions, plan changes, and invoices sync to HubSpot deals and companies, then reconcile MRR between the two with Finance before building reports on top of it.

requirements.need: Own or influence new-hire ramp time and onboarding metrics
requirements.evidence: I haven't owned ramp metrics. What I've built that bears on it: the AI proposal and agreement tools let new reps produce on-standard documents without memorizing the rules, and a grounded knowledge base (the pattern in this site's chat) is the obvious tool for cutting ramp time.

requirements.need: Product-led growth, upgrade paths, and monetization
requirements.evidence: Experimentation is the closest fit: I ran TRANZACT's A/B testing program (50% win rate, 30% CTR improvement) and built lifecycle data syncs into Iterable powering 10+ campaigns. I haven't owned PLG upgrade paths in a SaaS product.

featured.title: Resume Chat — a grounded knowledge base
featured.blurb: Answers come from one source document, retrieved by section and checked by an automated eval harness. It's the same pattern as an internal RevOps knowledge base that answers rep questions and cuts ramp time.

featured.title: From Attribution to Ad Spend
featured.blurb: How I turn overlapping, conflicting channel numbers into one budget decision: count each sale once, compare attribution models side by side, check them against lift tests, and reallocate in capped steps. Includes an interactive model.

featured.title: UTM Journey Tracker — live
featured.blurb: Data capture and governance in code: one controlled taxonomy, every record checked against it, failures counted by rule, and one channel definition every report reads from.

plan.phase: Days 1–30 · Map the stack and the money
items: Inventory every RevTech tool, its owner, cost, and what data it writes to HubSpot; flag overlaps and anything nobody can name an owner for.
Trace how a shop moves from lead to paying subscriber to renewal across HubSpot and Chargebee, and reconcile MRR between the two with Finance.
Meet each team lead (Marketing, Sales, CS, Finance, Partnerships) and my two direct reports to list the reports they rebuild by hand and the numbers they argue about.
Publish lifecycle-stage definitions and required fields agreed with every team, and enforce them in HubSpot with validation and dedup workflows.
Ship one funnel dashboard from first touch to paid and expansion, by segment, so the biggest leak is visible to the CRO and CFO.
Baseline new-hire ramp (time to first deal, time to quota) and launch a grounded internal knowledge base for reps on pricing, packaging, and process.
Present a consolidation plan with savings: tools to cut, merge, or replace, and the migration order.
Automate the highest-effort manual workflows with AI (record enrichment, lead scoring, renewal-risk flags), checked against the manual output before switching over.
Stand up a forecast model tied to HubSpot pipeline and Chargebee subscriptions, and report accuracy month over month.
